name: y2k-flash-scribble
note: Read by eye. keep = how it is made (copied verbatim); replace is set per slide.
keep: KEEP — the making of the image, copy exactly:

· PHOTOGRAPHY: a hyper-sharp editorial photograph shot with HARD DIRECT ON-CAMERA FLASH. Wet specular highlights, glossy surfaces, crushed shadow behind the subject, slightly over-sharpened. Fine film grain plus faint print noise over the whole frame.
· CROP: extreme close macro crop — the subject fills 100% of the frame and is cut by all four edges. No air around it.

· PAINTED SHAPES: irregular FLAT ULTRAMARINE BLUE blobs painted digitally ON TOP of the photograph with a rough dry brush — hard ragged edges, uneven coverage, opaque. They sit over the image like paint, ignoring what is underneath.
· SCRIBBLES: thin ACID GREEN hand-drawn squiggles and zigzags, jittery, drawn fast with a mouse, scattered across the whole frame at different scales.
· PALETTE: three saturated colours only — fire-engine red, ultramarine blue, acid green — over natural skin tone. Nothing muted, nothing pastel.
· HARDWARE: chrome-blue mirrored wraparound Y2K shield eyewear, metal piercings, gem-set teeth, black leather — glossy synthetic materials catching the flash.
· No readable text, no letters, no numerals, no logo, no watermark anywhere.
